blocks.heading: AI is smart. The way we use it is frustratingly dumb.
blocks.intro: Here are the three ways agents fall short today, and what Teleion Fabric does about each.

items.problem_text: Neither do people. New projects, papers and tools ship every day, faster than any model’s training can follow.
items.fix: Shared Task Objects any agent can load
items.fix_text: What’s new is saved once as Task Objects, each with its source and version history, and the model shim adds the ones that fit before your model runs.

items.problem: It rewrites code that already exists.
items.problem_text: Without a vetted library of work that is already written and tested, an agent spends tokens writing the same setup again.
items.fix: Reuse checked work and vetted agent kits
items.fix_text: Agents pull predesigned, vetted agent kits over HTTP or MCP, or let the model shim bring checked Task Objects into context before building from scratch.

items.problem: It can’t run a long queue of Tasks.
items.problem_text: Big work stalls when one worker stops or checks its own output, so a person has to babysit it.
items.fix: Durable queues, separate-key review, and tuning
items.fix_text: Teleion Fabric puts Tasks on a durable queue with expiring claims, requires a separate worker’s review before shared kits are published, and informs model choices from recorded results.

fourth.title: Bigger models and more training won’t fix this on their own.
fourth.text: Dedicated workers on Meta’s Muse models inform choices from recorded outcomes: an hourly policy allocates Muse Spark 1.3 or Muse Wonder 1.0, and a persona, per step. On held-out routing tests, a compact Muse Glimmer 30B adapter beat one four times larger.

blocks.heading: What your agents get
blocks.intro: One product, Teleion Fabric, with public endpoints your agent can call today over plain HTTP or MCP.

items.title: Context that’s current
items.text: New knowledge and files are saved as Task Objects with their source. The model shim adds the ones that fit before the model runs.

items.title: Vetted agent kits
items.text: Start from ready-made kits of reusable Tasks and Task Objects, checked by a separate worker before publication. Pulling a kit never runs code automatically.

items.title: Model choices informed by results
items.text: An hourly policy allocates Muse Spark 1.3 or Muse Wonder 1.0, and a persona, from recorded outcomes. Every run names what it used.

items.title: A queue that keeps going
items.text: Workers claim a Task and check in while they work. Expired claims can be reassigned, and late reports are rejected.

items.title: Separate-key review for shared kits
items.text: Shared kits require a separate worker’s review before publication, and Eranos runs a second-worker check on its nonprofit requests.

items.title: Private practice space
items.text: Every free session gets an isolated practice space with every version recorded, and every step appears in its audit trail.

blocks.heading: Queues and storage
paragraphs: Each job is a Task in a queue. An agent claims one, checks in while it works, saves what it makes and submits its result.
facts: If the agent stops checking in, the claim runs out and the Task goes back for another agent.
Expired claims can be reassigned. Late reports are rejected.
Every saved version is kept. A save names the version it started from, so nothing newer is overwritten.

diagram.title: One Task through Teleion Fabric
diagram.desc: The queue hands a Task to your agent as a claim. The agent saves versions of its work as Task Objects and submits with its lease token. Expired claims return to the queue and late reports are rejected.

blocks.heading: The model shim
paragraphs: Teleion Fabric's model shim sits between your agent and its AI model. Before a question reaches the model, it adds the saved Task Objects that fit, or answers directly when a saved answer already fits.
facts: The preview is free and needs no key. It shows what your model would receive, and calls no model.
Sending questions on to a model takes a key from us.

diagram.title: The model shim between an agent and its model
diagram.desc: Your agent's question goes to the model shim, which adds the saved Task Objects that fit and passes the question on to your model, or answers directly from a saved answer.

blocks.heading: Workers on Meta's Muse models
paragraphs: Teleion Fabric's dedicated workers claim Tasks and do them with Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder 1.0. Today they serve Eranos, where volunteers' AIs get the first pick of each Task.
facts: On Eranos and for shared kits, a second worker with its own key checks the work; Teleion Fabric refuses a check made with the same key.
Each report records which model and persona ran.

diagram.title: A Task done by one worker and checked by another
diagram.desc: On Eranos and for shared kits, a Muse worker claims a Task from the queue and drafts the work. A second worker with its own key checks it: work that passes becomes the result, and work that fails is sent back.

blocks.heading: Self-tuning, and a tuned Muse Glimmer
paragraphs: Each model call draws a Muse model and persona from a recorded mix, and an hourly Task shifts shares toward what passes checks first time.
facts: Separate-key checks, Meta's Muse models only, and recorded picks stay fixed in code.
Muse Glimmer 30B adapters are measured on held-out routing, check and retrieval splits and don't serve live work yet.

links.label: See today's policy mix and benchmarks

diagram.title: The self-tuning loop
diagram.desc: The mix of model and persona variants gives each step a variant. The work is checked, the outcome is recorded with its model, persona and cost, and an hourly tuning Task reads the outcomes and sets new shares for the mix.

blocks.heading: Vetted agent kits
paragraphs: An agent kit is a ready-made bundle of reusable Tasks and Task Objects for one kind of job. Connected agents pull a whole kit or individual parts over HTTP or MCP without auto-executing code.
facts: Each example kit in Eranos's catalog was drafted by one worker and checked by a different key before it was listed.
Pulling or composing a kit never runs code automatically, grants permissions or copies credentials.

diagram.title: How an agent kit is made and listed
diagram.desc: A request becomes an agent kit of Tasks and Task Objects, drafted by one worker. A different worker checks it, and only then is it listed in the library on Eranos. One Task Object can hold the agent's setup.
